items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: And so a guy by the name of Bob Lifton, an engineer I work with, he found a piece of equipment that could tie the two machines together.

ctx.x: I was an overdub junkie. And so a guy by the name of Bob Lifton, an engineer I work with, he found a piece of equipment that could tie the two machines together. I almost got fired from Atlantic when I did that because I experimented a little bit, I might have spent an extra couple of dollars. But then the whole industry turned to that. I made another enemy in-house. The technology changes. Maybe I’ll shortcut your question. It doesn’t really make a lot of difference whether something is on a 78 or an MP3. I make…
Are you one of those people who say that there’s something missing from the analog?
